import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Erdős Problem 946

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/946](https://www.erdosproblems.com/946)
 - [ErMi52] Erdős, P. and Mirsky, L., The distribution of values of the divisor function {$d(n)$}.
   Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) (1952), 257--271.
 - [Sp81] Spiro, C. A., The frequency with which an integral-valued, prime-independent,
   multiplicative or additive function of n divides a polynomial function of n.
 - [He84] Heath-Brown, D. R., The divisor function at consecutive integers.
   Mathematika 31 (1984), no. 2, 141--149.
 - [Hi85] Hildebrand, A., The divisor function at consecutive integers. Pacific J. Math.
   (1987), 307--319
 - [EPS87] Erdős, P., Pomerance, C., and Sarkőzy, A., On locally repeated values of
   arithmetic functions. III. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1987), 1--7.
-/

open Filter Real
open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos946

/--
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$. Proved in [He84].
Here τ is the divisor counting function, which is `σ 0` in mathlib.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n + 5040)$. Proved in [Sp81].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.spiro_5040 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 5040)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- Number of $n \le x$ with $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$. -/
noncomputable def erdos946Count (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ((Finset.range (⌊x⌋₊ + 1)).filter (fun n => σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1))).card

/--
The number of $n \le x$ with $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$ is at least $x / (\log x)^7$ for all sufficiently
large $x$. Proved in [He84].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.heathbrown_lower_bound :
    (fun x => x / (x.log)^7) =O[atTop] erdos946Count := by
  sorry

/--
Improved lower bound in [Hi85]: $Ω(x / (\log \log x)^3)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.hildebrand_lower_bound :
    (fun x => x / (x.log.log)^3) =O[atTop] erdos946Count := by
  sorry

/--
Upper bound in [EPS87]: $O(x / \sqrt{\log \log x})$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.upper_bound : erdos946Count =O[atTop] (fun x => x / √x.log.log ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos946

findings.description: The docstring says the count is eventually at least x/(log x)^7, with coefficient 1. The Lean statement instead gives a lower bound up to an unspecified positive multiplicative constant. The Lean statement matches the cited result; only the prose overstates what this declaration asserts.
findings.source_evidence: Hildebrand, The divisor function at consecutive integers, p. 307, equation (1.1), states Heath-Brown's bound using ≫. EPS87, p. 1, likewise says 'at least order of magnitude x/(log x)^7 solutions'. See https://msp.org/pjm/1987/129-2/pjm-v129-n2-p06-s.pdf and https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-15.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to 'at least a positive constant multiple of x/(log x)^7 for all sufficiently large x', or use ≫. Leave the Lean statement unchanged.

findings.description: The bibliography entry [He84] gives Mathematika 31 (1984), no. 2, pp. 141–149. The cited article appeared in issue 1, not issue 2. This does not affect the mathematical statements.
findings.source_evidence: Cambridge's article record identifies Volume 31, Issue 1, June 1984, pp. 141–149: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematika/article/abs/divisor-function-at-consecutive-integers/D77FEA48858ED5238A2AD4CC6AD2C338.

reformulations.difference: The implementation uses a range beginning at zero and a natural-valued floor on all real inputs, rather than explicitly counting positive integers n ≤ x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A solution of σ 0 n = σ 0 (n+1) has n > 0, since σ 0 0 = 0 and σ 0 1 = 1. For nonzero n, Nat.le_floor_iff' gives n ≤ ⌊x⌋₊ iff (n : ℝ) ≤ x, even when x is negative. The scratch lemma counted_iff proves that membership in the filtered range is exactly 0 < n ∧ (n : ℝ) ≤ x ∧ σ 0 n = σ 0 (n+1), for every real x. Thus the count agrees exactly with the intended count, including boundary cases.

reformulations.difference: The source writes N(x) ≫ x/(log x)^7; Lean places the comparison function on the left of =O and the count on the right.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The count is nonnegative, and x/(log x)^7 is nonnegative for sufficiently large x. Consequently Mathlib's norm-based big-O statement is equivalent to ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, c * (x/(log x)^7) ≤ N(x). This precise equivalence was proved in the scratch file and matches the source's ≫ bound.

reformulations.difference: The source's lower bound N(x) ≫ x/(log log x)^3 is expressed using reversed big-O rather than lower-bound notation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both functions are eventually nonnegative. Using Asymptotics.isBigO_iff'', the Lean statement is equivalent to ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ x in atTop, c * (x/(log log x)^3) ≤ N(x). This was proved in the scratch file. The double logarithm is explicitly confirmed by Hildebrand's abstract and Theorem 1.

review.notes: All six declarations were checked. No mathematical misformalizations or status discrepancies were found; the findings above are documentation-only. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully and verifies the counting-domain equivalence, positivity restrictions for both infinitude statements, all three asymptotic-bound interpretations, and the square-root parsing. Computed counts at 100, 1000, and 10000 are 15, 118, and 1119. The independent equivalence lemmas do not use the problem file's sorry axioms. The target file remains unchanged. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/946 was blocked by Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers; Spiro's thesis and Heath-Brown's full text were not retrieved. Their precise results were corroborated in the cited Hildebrand and EPS87 papers, while the original conjecture was read in Erdős–Mirsky and the proved status was checked in the Erdős community database.
